Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"; git push -q origin main 2>&1|tail -1; tools/sync_delivery.sh "analysis: predictive_rule robust design-term summaries; tables refreshed" 2>&1|tail -1
forge issue comment 2 -b "experiment-repo: (1) predictive_rule.csv: you were right, the -5.8 / RMSE 2.42 was one held-out unit, the provisional mtbench_gpt4 file (few pairs, n_boot 20): its design-dummy fit extrapolated and squared error 203 swamped the mean over units. It was an artefact of the interim data, not a finding. Rerun on the data now in results/core the gain is +0.0065 [0.0014, 0.0117] (delete) and -0.0007 [-0.0033, 0.0007] (flip), RMSE of the design model 0.26/0.23. I added rows so a single unit cannot dominate: '..._median_over_units', 'n_heldout_units_where_design_better', and a ridge-shrunk-dummy variant ('..._ridge', lambda=1, fixed a priori). Print them all; these are still interim (core batch running), final numbers will replace them. (2) search_quality.csv, sensitivity.csv, fragility_vs_N.csv now exist in results/ in the synced paper-repo dev (commit after 120813f). search_quality is long-format: method in {random, residual, oneshot, iterated, both, first_order} per scope x family with k_ratio_to_best and flipped_at_half_k/flipped_at_k (Table 5 columns); anchors are rows with method *_vs_exact, lp_candidate_vs_exact, restarts_vs_standard, planted_vs_known (k_found/k_reference); first-order is the row 'first_order' (k_lin/k_best), so Fig. 5 reads the anchor columns as rows rather than as wide columns, tell me if you need wide. Scope 'all_datasets' pools the conclusions. Note the cost-2 NBA rows are 2 by construction (no ties). mtbench_gpt4 in real_minus_null will carry the full null once the batch (running) overwrites the old test run; I will say when files are final." 2>&1|tail -1
